summary: This lecture continues the Prophet's ﷺ childhood after his return from Banu Sa'd: ages four to six with his mother Aminah, the journey to Yathrib, Aminah's death at Al-Abwa', the care of Abdul Muttalib, who exposed him to the gatherings of leaders, then the entrusting to Abu Talib and the role of Fatimah bint Asad. The ustaz explains the wisdom of the Prophet's ﷺ orphanhood: he was trained to depend only on Allah, to live with very little wealth, and it was clear that his message was no shortcut to power. He then discusses the meaning of yatim, the rights of orphans, the importance of love and attachment over merely giving food, drink and shelter, and the hadiths that encourage caring for orphans.
keyPoints: The Prophet ﷺ lost his father before birth, his mother at age six and his grandfather at age eight, yet there was always an adult caring for him.
Abdul Muttalib exposed the Prophet ﷺ to gatherings of leaders from an early age and spoke words that built his confidence.
Abdul Muttalib chose Abu Talib to care for the Prophet ﷺ because he valued character and tarbiah over wealth.
The Prophet's ﷺ orphanhood trained him to depend only on Allah, to live simply, and made clear that his message was not for gaining power and wealth.
Orphans need love and an adult who is attached to them, not merely food, drink and a roof.
Standing up for orphans is the mark of one who does not deny the faith, and it is done regardless of the child's religion.

chapters.title: Opening: high aspirations in dua
chapters.summary: The ustaz reminds us to aim high, including martyrdom, and to leave the how to Allah, like the dua of Umar al-Khattab.

chapters.title: Recap and the ninth episode marker
chapters.summary: Recalls the Prophet ﷺ having his chest opened and being sent home by Halimah, and notes that one tenth of the series journey has been covered.

chapters.title: The Prophet ﷺ with his mother Aminah
chapters.summary: Almost nothing is recorded from age four to six, and Aminah did not remarry because she devoted herself to the Prophet ﷺ.

chapters.title: The journey to Yathrib
chapters.summary: Aminah took the Prophet ﷺ and Umm Ayman to Yathrib, where he met his grandmother's side of the family and stayed about a month.

chapters.title: The death of Aminah at Al-Abwa'
chapters.summary: On the way back Aminah fell ill at Al-Abwa' and died, and the Prophet ﷺ lost his mother at age six.

chapters.title: Umm Ayman and the weeping at his mother's grave
chapters.summary: Umm Ayman looked after the Prophet ﷺ, and a hadith in Muslim tells how he wept very hard at his mother's grave.

chapters.title: Cared for by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ was received by his aged grandfather, given a special seat and encouraging words.

chapters.title: The lost camel and Abdul Muttalib's love
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ was sent to find a lost camel, and Abdul Muttalib was so worried that he vowed never to let him out of his sight again.

chapters.title: Early exposure to gatherings of leaders
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ sat with Abdul Muttalib when tribal chiefs visited, and the ustaz links this to the story of Prophet Yusuf AS as a servant in Al-Aziz's house.

chapters.title: What shapes a leader, according to Tariq Suwaidan
chapters.summary: Early exposure, the first six years and orphanhood are discussed as factors that build leadership character, and most leaders are made, not born.

chapters.title: The bequest to Abu Talib
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib chose Abu Talib because tarbiah matters more than wealth, even though other uncles were richer.

chapters.title: Abu Talib's family and Fatimah bint Asad
chapters.summary: The ustaz names Abu Talib's six children, their modest living, and the role of Fatimah bint Asad as the Prophet's ﷺ second mother. The Prophet ﷺ calmly waited his turn to eat, and Abu Talib saw blessing when he ate with them.

chapters.title: The wisdom of the Prophet's ﷺ orphanhood
chapters.summary: Allah trained the Prophet to depend only on Him and to live with very little wealth.

chapters.title: The meaning of yatim and the orphanage concept
chapters.summary: A yatim is one who lost his father before reaching puberty, orphans need attachment, and the ustaz cites studies on the effect of missing affection.

chapters.title: Hadiths on caring for orphans
chapters.summary: The hadith of the two fingers in Paradise, softening the heart by caring for an orphan, and the reward of those who care for widows and the poor.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Ma'un and closing
chapters.summary: Turning away an orphan is a sign of denying the faith, orphans are defended regardless of religion, and the Prophet fought for them to his last breath.

Cited on the wisdom of Allah making the Prophet an orphan, so that it would be clear his mission was not to gain power and wealth.

books.context: One of the sources for Abu Talib's account of the Prophet being more mature than other children.

people.context: Prayed for martyrdom in Madinah, and Allah arranged it when he was stabbed while leading the Fajr prayer.

people.role: The one who stabbed Umar RA

Did not remarry after Abdullah and devoted her attention to the Prophet ﷺ, before dying at Al-Abwa' on the way back from Yathrib.
Accompanied Aminah and the Prophet ﷺ to Yathrib, comforted him when Aminah died, and moved with him into Abu Talib's house.
Cared for the Prophet ﷺ attentively, let him sit on his special seat, exposed him to gatherings of leaders, and bequeathed his care to Abu Talib.
Used as an example: his exposure as a servant in Al-Aziz's house shaped his ability to manage an economy.

people.role: Foster mother of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Among those who told of the Prophet's ﷺ maturity beyond his years.

people.role: Author of the Encyclopedia of Sirah
people.context: Argues that the first six years and orphanhood shape the character of a leader, and set up childcare centres built on leadership values.
Richer and better placed financially, but not chosen by Abdul Muttalib to care for the Prophet ﷺ.
His real name was Abdul Manaf. Chosen by Abdul Muttalib to care for the Prophet for his character, although his business was not profitable.
The first two sons of Abu Talib, and Talib is why he was called Abu Talib.

people.role: Son of Abu Talib and Companion
people.context: Would migrate to Abyssinia and die a martyr, given wings in Paradise, and the Prophet ﷺ would greet him with extraordinary emotion.

people.role: Son of Abu Talib and Companion
people.context: The fourth son of Abu Talib, who will appear often in the sirah to come.
One of Abu Talib's two daughters.
The last of Abu Talib's six children.
The Prophet's ﷺ second mother, one of the earliest women to embrace Islam and migrate; she died in Madinah and the Prophet himself shrouded her, prayed over her and buried her.
A non-Muslim author whose book helps one sense the loneliness of the Prophet ﷺ as an orphan.
Complained that his heart was hard, and the Prophet taught him to show mercy to orphans.
Narrated the hadith on the reward of those who care for widows and the poor.

Mentioned by Tariq Suwaidan among great figures who grew up without a father.

lessons.title: Aim high in your aspirations
lessons.body: We pray and aspire big, and Allah fulfils it in the way He wills.

lessons.title: Give children space and building words
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib defended the Prophet ﷺ on his seat and spoke of his great future, so that a child has a high picture of himself.

lessons.title: Expose children to big conversations
lessons.body: Rather than shooing children away when guests come, teach them manners and let them sit and watch how adults discuss.

lessons.title: A leader's environment shapes leaders
lessons.body: One becomes a leader more easily when raised among leaders, because early exposure gives an advantage.

lessons.title: Leaders are made and trained
lessons.body: Only a few are born leaders, the rest are shaped and trained, so we should build leadership from childhood.

lessons.title: Character matters more than wealth
lessons.body: Choose a child's guardian not by riches but by the ability to educate, lead and care.

lessons.title: Highest reliance is on Allah alone
lessons.body: Orphanhood trained the Prophet ﷺ to rely on Allah, not on people, including parents and uncles.

lessons.title: Live with little wealth
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ was trained to live with little so that when this world and the next collide, wealth does not sit in his heart.

lessons.title: Orphans need love, not just food and drink
lessons.body: An orphan needs an adult attached to him who cares for his soul, not just food, clothing and a dormitory.

lessons.title: Beware of the name and wealth of orphans
lessons.body: An orphan is not an eligible zakat recipient unless poor, the name 'orphan' is sometimes used to raise donations, and consuming his wealth is a major sin.

lessons.title: Care for orphans in your own home
lessons.body: Caring for an orphan means eating and living together with us, not merely patting his head at an annual event and sending him back.

lessons.title: Defend orphans regardless of religion
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ defended orphans in Makkah whether Muslim or not, so we too defend them unconditionally.

lessons.title: Discipline orphans like your own children
lessons.body: Do not leave an orphan undisciplined out of fear he will be spoiled, but care for and educate him like your own child.

lessons.title: The message is no shortcut to power
lessons.body: The Prophet's ﷺ life from childhood shows he defended principle, and cannot be accused of reaching power by shortcuts.

lessons.title: Honour the mothers behind great figures
lessons.body: Behind figures like Imam Bukhari are mothers who raised and educated them, and their reward keeps flowing.

glossary.meaning: A noble death in the cause of Allah, which believers aspire to.
A group of traders travelling together, most likely how Aminah travelled to Yathrib.
Educating, guiding and caring for someone.
The Malay term for a child who lost both father and mother.
A child who lost his father before reaching puberty. Losing only the mother does not make one a yatim in the Qur'anic sense.
Reaching adulthood in Islamic law, at which point one is no longer counted as an orphan.
A child attached to an adult who cares for him and settles his soul, which orphans need more than food and drink.
The categories of people entitled to receive zakat. An orphan is not one unless he is poor.

dalil.context: The ustaz reminds us that we pray and aspire high, and the how is Allah's affair, like the dua of Umar al-Khattab.
dalil.translation: All of us should aspire to a noble death, which is martyrdom.

dalil.context: The one narration often cited about the Prophet's ﷺ mother, which took place about eight years after the Hijrah.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ stopped at a grave and wept so hard that the Companions wept with him. He explained it was the grave of his mother Aminah, and that he had asked Allah's permission to visit it and was granted it.

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses how serious it is to consume an orphan's wealth.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned seven major sins, one of which is consuming the wealth of orphans.

dalil.context: Allah describes consuming an orphan's wealth unjustly as putting fire in one's belly. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are actually swallowing fire into their own bellies: they will burn in the blazing Flame.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ showed how close the one who cares for an orphan will be to him in Paradise.
dalil.translation: I and the one who cares for an orphan will be in Paradise like this, and the Prophet ﷺ held up his two fingers.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains this means caring for the orphan and eating together in one's own home, not merely patting his head at an event.
dalil.translation: A Companion complained that his heart was hard. The Prophet ﷺ offered something that softens the heart and fulfils needs: have mercy on the orphan, stroke his head and feed him from your own food.

dalil.context: Widows who raise orphans, and the poor, are among the weakest groups.
dalil.translation: One who strives to support widows and the poor is like one who fights in the cause of Allah, like one who fasts by day without breaking and prays by night without sleeping.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ stressed the rights of the weak, and the Companions competed to care for orphans.
dalil.translation: I have conveyed to you the rights of orphans and women.

dalil.context: Surah Al-Ma'un begins by mentioning the one who denies the faith. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: [Prophet], have you considered the person who denies the Judgement?

dalil.context: The first mark of one who denies the faith is that he turns away or pushes aside the orphan. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: It is he who pushes aside the orphan

dalil.context: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that he was once an orphan and Allah gave him shelter. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you?

dalil.context: The Companions feared that orphans would become spoiled or naughty if not disciplined.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ answered a Companion worried about disciplining an orphan: discipline them as you discipline your own child, and look after them like your own child.

sirah.era: The Prophet's ﷺ childhood: an orphan in Makkah
sirah.summary: The Prophet returns to Aminah, goes with her to Yathrib, loses his mother at Al-Abwa', is cared for by Abdul Muttalib, then entrusted to Abu Talib.

events.label: Age 6
events.title: Journey to Yathrib
events.desc: Aminah took the Prophet and Umm Ayman to his grandmother's family, and they stayed about a month.

events.label: Age 6
events.title: Aminah dies at Al-Abwa'
events.desc: On the way back Aminah fell ill and died as the Prophet looked on, after entrusting him to Umm Ayman.

events.label: After Al-Abwa'
events.title: Cared for by Abdul Muttalib
events.desc: Umm Ayman brought the Prophet back to Makkah, where his grandfather received and cared for him.

events.label: Age 7 to 8
events.title: Searching for the lost camel
events.desc: Abdul Muttalib sent the Prophet to find his camel as training, and was very worried when he returned late.

events.label: Age 8
events.title: The bequest to Abu Talib
events.desc: The ailing Abdul Muttalib entrusted the Prophet to Abu Talib.

events.label: Age 8
events.title: Moving to Abu Talib's house
events.desc: The Prophet joined Abu Talib's family and was looked after by Fatimah bint Asad.

events.label: Age 8 to 12
events.title: Four years with no major record
events.desc: The sirah books record no significant event, only attentive care.

mindmap.label: The Prophet ﷺ grew up an orphan
mindmap.detail: Loss after loss, yet always cared for, and the wisdom shaped a leader and teaches us to care for orphans.
